summary.title: Trouble hiring senior engineers? It's probably you
summary.one_liner: When hiring senior engineers the candidate chooses the company, so job posts, company information, and the interview process should be written and run as selling rather than buying.
takeaways: Senior engineers have many options, so the company must sell its offer rather than just list its requirements.
Job postings that list mostly needs and requirements, with few benefits, fail to catch candidates' attention.
Make key company details such as team organization, management style, and working hours easy to find before the interview.
Run interviews on time, well prepared, and friendly, and keep decisions quick without being pushy.
Keep programming assessments short and close to real work, letting candidates use their own laptop and ask questions.
summary.summary: The author argues that hiring senior software engineers is a selling exercise, since strong candidates have many offers. He critiques typical job postings (mostly requirements, few benefits), hard-to-find company information, and slow, disorganized interviews, using a computer-buying analogy. He recommends being on time, prepared, friendly, and quick with decisions, and making any technical assessment short, realistic, and collaborative. The post is opinion-based and includes a few personal anecdotes rather than data.
